_comment: Phase 140.2-09 / TS-04 — the committed case table for the X-Tenant-Claim wire format.
WHY A FILE AND NOT A LITERAL IN EACH SUITE. The TypeScript mint
(src/lib/tenant-claim.ts) and the Python verifier
(analytics-service/services/rate_limit.py:verify_tenant_claim) cannot import each
other. A copy-pasted literal in each suite proves only that someone once copied
correctly; a committed fixture binds both readers to the SAME BYTES, so a drift on
either side reddens the other's suite. This is the same shape as
analytics-service/tests/fixtures/process_key_onboard_contract.json, which
tests/lib/process-key-onboard-contract-parity.test.ts and
analytics-service/tests/test_process_key_onboard_contract.py already share.
PROVENANCE OF THE `claim` VALUES. Each was computed ONCE by a standalone
`node -e` process calling node:crypto directly — never by importing the module
under test. An oracle that asks the code under test what it expects cannot fail.
WIRE FORMAT: `<payload>.<exp>.<hex-hmac-sha256>`, MAC over `"<payload>.<exp>"`,
key = INTERNAL_API_TOKEN. `exp` = floor(now/1000) + ttl_seconds. The Python parse
is `raw.rsplit(".", 2)`, so the payload must contain no dot (the TS mint refuses
one) and the claim must be <= 512 characters.
⚠️ OWED: a pytest reader bound to THIS file. Phase 146 owns the limiter surface;
see 140.1-TS-OBLIGATIONS.md TS-36. Until that lands the cross-language gate rests
on the single hand-copied literal 140.1 pinned in
analytics-service/tests/test_process_key.py, not on this table.

cases.name: tenant-a
cases.why: the A half of the cross-tenant isolation pair — same clock, same secret, different payload

cases.name: tenant-b
cases.why: the B half — its MAC must differ from tenant-a's, which is what makes the buckets separate

cases.name: uuid-payload
cases.why: the production shape: a Supabase user.id is a dot-free UUID

cases.name: public-anonymous-different-secret
cases.why: the teaser bucket payload, and a DIFFERENT secret — pins that the key is an input, not a constant
